corrections: Replaced generic transport with dimensioned DC-3 shell, faceted oval sections, seven passenger windows per side, right-side entrance, swept outer-wing leading edges and broad rounded tail.
Authored Wright Cyclone single-row nine-cylinder engines, pushrods/cooling fins, short metal cowls, three-blade Hamilton Standard hubs, nacelle contours, exhausts and induction scoops.
Added main-gear retraction, differential27/18-degree ailerons,30/20-degree elevator,30-degree rudder and45-degree split flaps; independent control surfaces and engine RPM sources.

Rebuilt Knoxville panel from Highsmith photograph, paired flight clusters, shared two-needle RPM dial, six-lever pedestal, white trim wheel, split wheels, pedals, overhead ignition/switch bank and21-seat2+1cabin.

Overlay and close-view corrections include wing-tip trailing edges, tail root chord, nacelle upper contour, tailwheel height, segmented window apertures, roof/overhead fit, rising aft floor and lettering below windows.
reviewNotes.visual: Personally inspected all four current overlays, eight standard renders and twelve detail/state captures after final geometry corrections. Compared outline stations, planform, nacelles, gear and panel layout against original manual and photographs; checked zero/cruise/limits/missing telemetry, both control directions, gear-up, overhead, lower controls, close exterior and passenger cabin.
limitations: Manual drawing covers UAL P&W-powered DC-3/DST; only common airframe dimensions/geometry/control travel used. Modeled Wright cowls and cockpit come from Knoxville photographs. This is not an exact serial-number restoration.
Scanned three-view has small plan/side dimension discrepancies; printed95ft span and64ft5.5in length take priority. No nonuniform overlay fitting.

Cockpit dimensions and high forward pilot viewpoint are estimates from perspective photos and available fuselage volume, not a surveyed ergonomic model. Lower obscured gauges and switch labels are simplified.
The11.5-degree tailwheel stance is baked into the asset; the assisted simulation does not independently raise the tail to the flight datum. Gear linkages approximate the retraction path.

Live gauges show simulated true airspeed in mph, geometric altitude in feet, true heading, pitch/roll, vertical speed, yaw rate, flap position and independent normalized engine RPM scaled to2350. No IAS/barometric/magnetic/gyro-error or propeller-governor simulation is claimed.

Manifold/oil/fuel/temperature/vacuum/navigation/clock systems are unmodeled and have no fabricated readings. Propeller, mixture, trim and overhead switches are static; only throttle levers follow shared power input.
Cabin liner, seating and airframe rivet courses are polygonal approximations; no source photograph pixels are embedded or redistributed.

cockpitReview.method: packages/entities/scripts/cockpit-sweep.mjs rays from pilotEye through source.glb, then seat, pitched-down and exterior nose renders inspected at the runtime camera (+Z, 60 degrees vertical).
corrections: No seat stood under the eye: the seats sat on a low floor 2.1 m below it and aft of it. A raised flight deck at y 2.9 now carries seats, column bases and pedals, with the eye over the cushion at [0.56, 4.2, 7.25] in the airframe datum.
Overhead panel faced up and aft near the head. It now follows the sloping roof behind the header, facing the pilots, at 72 percent width to fit under the curved ceiling.

Compass housing stood outside the windscreen; it moved behind the header and shrank to a 90 mm card. Panel lowered 0.1 m and its outer corners clipped so it stays inside the skin. Side quilting pulled inside the shell.
Bare-aluminium roof read as a black mass from inside, so the deck roof gained a painted lining.
limitations: Deck height is inferred from the seated eye and the fuselage section, not from a drawing; no cockpit floor plan was found. The overhead width is a fit to the modeled ceiling, not a measurement. Horizon 41 percent reflects the 11.5 degree tail-down stance.
